title: The reshimu and the Kav: the Essence that makes the rules and can break them
overview:
The last chapter's analogies now meet their *nimshal*. After the *tzimtzum* G-d left a *reshimu*, an impression that holds His whole *etzem*, but as a *hiyuli*, a point that could become anything, and so in itself it shows nothing: a tree is a tree, a rock is a rock, ink is ink. He is seen through the *Kav*, His choice imposing an order, as a soul is seen in the movements of a body and a squirrel's forgotten acorns plant the forest.

The *Kav* holds two opposites. It unites everything, even *chesed* in the vessel of *gevura*, and it is the *kav hamida* that measures every light and vessel. Both are true, because it comes from the *Atzmus*, and whoever makes the rules can break them: the teacher with his class plan, the architect with his blueprint, the husband who can change the pool room. So every change, from weekday to *Shabbos* and from the *Beis HaMikdash* to *galus*, comes from the Essence, and we pray to Him, not to His *middos*. Two Q and A tapes bring it down to squirrels, coffee, nerves and cells.

sections.title: The reshimu: everything hidden in a point, so the world looks separate
sections.summary: The *reshimu* left after the *tzimtzum* holds G-d's whole *etzem*, but as a *hiyuli* that could become anything, so in itself it reveals nothing and the world looks separate from Him. He is seen only through the *Kav*: His choice, the order and the changes He imposes, as a soul is seen in the movements of a body.

blocks.text:
**Now the analogue, the real point of everything that we said until now**: not really everything, just the last chapter. The last chapter spoke about the *Kav* (the line of light), and also about how the *Kav* can come out from the *reshimu* (the impression left after the *tzimtzum*). That was the question: how do you get a *Kav* out of a *reshimu*? A *reshimu* is a complete *helem* (concealment), where everything is hidden, and a *Kav* is a *gilui* (revelation). How can the light start coming out of it as a *Kav* if it is totally hidden?

We said that they are not really opposites. Put a bunch of points together and you get a line. A point is like a *koach hahiyuli* (raw potential), the essence of what everything is built out of. That it has no *gilui* and no *hispashtus* (spreading forth) is not because it cannot reveal anything, but because it is the essence everything comes out from, so it could reveal anything, and therefore it does not come out in any particular way. A point you can make lines out of; when you just have a point, you can do anything with it.

So what is the *nimshal* (what the analogy stands for)? The *reshimu* is that G-d makes a *tzimtzum* (contraction) in the way of a *siluk* (removal), where He hides His whole *or* (light). His light means Himself: He hides His *etzem* (essence). You do not see it as His *etzem*; you see it as something separate from His *etzem*. G-d hides His *etzem* and leaves something that looks like a separate thing, and you just have those *osios* (letters).

That is the idea that G-d made a *tzimtzum* and left a *chalal reikan* and *makom panui* (an empty space, a vacant place): He left a potential for something to appear separate from Him. In that potential to create a world is everything, all the different things G-d could make, but seen as something separate, the form of how they would be. That is the idea of the *roshem*, **the impression**.

So practically for us: when you look at the world and see it as something separate, you are just seeing the *reshimu*. You look at the world and do not see its connection to G-d, and it seems like an isolated point, points that are separate.

blocks.title: The yud of SaG
blocks.text:
This is a kabbalistic digression, which is why it is in parentheses: **this reshimu is the yud of the name SaG** (the Name of sixty-three). Spell out the letters of *SaG*, and the last *yud*, the one of the last *hei*, is the idea of the *reshimu*.

How does it work? At first G-d made the *tzimtzum* in a way that is round: He removed His *etzem or*, the light that is *b'li gvul* (without limit). There are two parts to the *tzimtzum*: the *siluk* of the unlimited light, and a *miut* (lessening) of the limited light. There is something called *olam hamalbush*, the world of the garment, and that is a square *makif* (encompassing light), the root of the *tallis*, the *sukka* and all the things that are square. So first G-d made the round *tzimtzum*. Then inside the *makom panui* He made the *hashara* (estimation) of how everything would be, and it says that it was like a square woven of letters: all the *osios*, the root of the limited light, the root of *memalei kol almin*, the *hashara* of everything G-d could make in the world. Those are the Names *Ayin Beis*, *SaG*, *MaH* and *BaN* in the corners.

blocks.title: Folding the square of letters
blocks.text: First there is *Ayin Beis*, next to it *SaG*, then *MaH*, and then *BaN*: those are the four corners. Then G-d took that square and folded it over onto itself, and each letter paired up with another letter and became hidden by the pairing. But the Name *BaN* has only nine letters, and the other three Names have ten. *MaH* paired up with *Ayin Beis* and *BaN* with *SaG*, so when He folded it over, the last *yud* of *SaG* had no pair and was left sticking out. That *yud* is the *reshimu*.

blocks.title: From the middle to the top
blocks.text:
So there are really two *reshimus*. First there is the circle *tzimtzum*, which leaves a *roshem* in the middle of the *chalal*. Then G-d blew that *roshem* up into the square, folded it over, and left this *yud*, another *nekuda* (point), now at the top corner, touching the circle on the far corner. The *Kav* comes down from that point; that is its starting point.

Did you ever wonder how the *reshimu* got from the middle to the top for the *Kav* to come out of it? Rabbi Walters always wondered. It says the point is left in the middle, but then it says the *Kav* comes out from it, from the top. "So I'm like, what's going on? How did it get from the middle to the top?" This is how.

blocks.title: To one side
blocks.text: The other thing: in *Tanya*, chapter 45 he thinks, it says something about *siluk*, that G-d was *metzamtzem* (contracted) His light to one side, *l'tzad echad*. Why one side? He should have said all sides, since a circle is all around. The answer is that there he is talking about this square *tzimtzum*, folded over to one side. The Mitteler Rebbe will explain the square later, when he talks about *bina* (understanding). All of this is parentheses: "That was our kabbalistic digression for those that are interested."

blocks.text:
**This roshem is a hiyuli that includes everything that's going to come out from it in the Kav.** Everything that comes out of the *Kav* is only a *gilui* of what was already hidden in the *reshimu*. It is nothing new; it only brings out particular things.

Like the *mashal* (analogy) of the teacher: all his knowledge is hidden in his mind, his memories, a *roshem*, and then he brings out particular explanations, each one like a little *Kav*. They are only revealed out of all his knowledge, put together in different ways. And you could put it together in infinite ways, which is why it is a *hiyuli*: just as you can take points and put them together in any shape, the *osios* he knows he can arrange in all different shapes.

phrases.he: וגם שנתעלם כללות האור העצמות
phrases.en: but even though the general *or* of the *Atzmus* was hidden by the *tzimtzum*,

phrases.he: עם כל זה ודאי הכל נכלל בו בקיצור

phrases.he: על ידי זה הצמצום דווקא
phrases.en: through this very *tzimtzum*,

phrases.he: כנזכר לעיל

blocks.text:
**But even though the general or of the Atzmus was hidden by the tzimtzum**, **until only an impression was left**, so that you do not see it in these *osios*: the whole point of the *tzimtzum* is that now the *osios* can be given over to a student, and seen as independent of the teacher's mind. Before the *tzimtzum* you do not see the letters of the teacher's knowledge as separate from his mind: he understands it, this is what he understands, and it is all one thing. Now he takes that information and makes it as if it were independent of him, so he can explain it to you. You do not have to be him or understand everything; he can just tell you the facts. The knowledge is really hidden in there, but now in a way that seems separate.

So too in the *nimshal*: G-d makes the world look like a separate thing, but really it is *mamash* (actually) G-d Himself, *mamash* the *Atzmus*.

The *tzimtzum* is not *kipshuto* (literal), and in the *nimshal* that means that really everything is G-d, as before the *tzimtzum*. The *tzimtzum* is not a place; that is the reality. The question is only how it looks separate, and it only looks separate, because it is not literal. G-d is *kol yachol* (all-capable), so He hid the fact that it is Him. He has the power of both: He can show you what it would be like if He were not there, and He can make Himself be in a limited way. So you see different things. The point is not so much that they are different, since you could see different things and still see them as G-d; it is that you do not see them as connected to Him anymore. That is what G-d wanted: that you should not see the world as essentially connected to Him.

blocks.title: The soul seen in the body's movements
blocks.text:
How then do you see it connected to Him? Through the *Kav*. The *Kav* is like His *bechira* (choice): He is controlling it, and from the fact that He changes things, departs from the order, you see that there is a G-d there.

Like a person's body: the soul's control of the body reveals his *etzem* in the body. You see that there is a person there, though the body is a totally separate thing, not a soul at all; the movements show that there is an intellect, there is emotion. Take a person at any one second and look at his body in its state at that moment: it is a dead, physical thing. The next moment it is still a dead, physical thing. The soul is never revealed in the physicality of the body. That is why time is the intermediary between *olam* (world) and *nefesh* (soul): since the G-dliness of the world comes in a *Kav*, the soul is revealed through the changes that happen.

In the same way, the vitality, the G-dliness in the world, that there is a *ratzon* (will), a higher being, an intellect, you see mainly from the changes that happen over time: how everything is working and is run with a purpose. Even in one moment, if you contrast all the differences between things, that also shows you a *nefesh*.

So first you have to see how you would see it as separate. You see a tree, and that is it, an isolated point: a tree is a tree, a squirrel is a squirrel, the world is a world. The very fact that there is an existence that is separate is just a point. But once you are seeing a tree you are already seeing a *Kav*, because it was put in a certain form; it is already a bunch of points, the roots and the trunk and the branches, infinite points. So you already see a big intellect there, a purpose, and from the differentiations you see that there is something higher. Putting the points together into a tree is already making a *Kav*, and the more you put together, the more you start to see.

blocks.title: The squirrel that forgets its acorns
blocks.text: Then you start seeing the relationships, the symbiotic relationship between the trees and the animals and the bugs. The other day Rabbi Walters saw a squirrel burying an acorn. "What does it think it's doing? I don't know what it thinks it's doing." Officially, people say they are hiding them for after the winter, and they go running around grabbing acorns, digging a little hole and burying them; "it's kind of cute the way they do it." But the problem is that they do not remember where they put them, so they cannot find them after the winter. Say they get lucky and find some; it is not that they remember. So it cannot be that they do it for themselves: what is the point of burying them if you do not remember? G-d *davka* (specifically) makes them want to go hide them, and then they forget, so that they plant the trees. They work for the tree: they carry the seeds around and bury them, plant them.

blocks.title: G-d's cleanup crew
blocks.text: Look at everything in the world: all these bugs and bacteria and all kinds of different things, and they all do stuff, like little workers. Sometimes there are some crumbs on his floor and he sees ants going and taking them: "it's like G-d sends these little cleanup crew guys to come in and take out the stuff." They have their job, and when there is leftover food lying around, they go and take it away and turn it into something useful.

**Even though it's only reshimu, surely everything is hidden there in a short way**, **through this very tzimtzum**: the *tzimtzum* stuffs everything into the *reshimu*; it does not take it away. It puts it in by way of *kitzur* (shortening), hiding it all inside the *reshimu*.

What does that mean? It means that G-d is *metzamtzem* Himself: this is what He is. He decided that He is going to be a squirrel. That is really what we are saying, that it is *mamash* Him: His whole *etzem* is there, but you just do not see it.

blocks.title: He's hurting this piece of meat
blocks.text: It is like the soul coming into the body. On the one hand it comes into the body, and so you say that the body is *mamash* you; that is why you get angry if somebody hurts your body, because it is you. "He's hurting me." "What do you mean, he's hurting me? He's hurting this piece of meat." "No, but it's me, it's not just a piece of meat." So on the one hand you say it is you. On the other hand it is not you, because no matter what a person does to your body, it is not going to hurt the soul. The soul cannot be killed or hurt or maimed.

So too with G-d, and it is a one-way thing: He is not *mamash nitfas* (caught). G-d decided to become a squirrel, but He did not become trapped and turn into a squirrel. He is still G-d, higher than the squirrel, revealing Himself through the form of a squirrel. He is showing you that He is higher than any form, and therefore He can reveal Himself in any form.
"You know, the great unknowable beyond is no better than a squirrel. Come on, it's pretty lame, the great unknowable beyond. I know some squirrels that are better than that."

So He is not *mamash* stuck in it, and that is why you cannot bow down to something: that would be *avoda zara* (idol worship). Why? Because it is not that the thing is G-d. It is a one-way thing: it is Him, but the way your body is you. It is not *mamash* you; it is you only when you realize that you are something higher, and yet you are *mamash* in your body.

So first of all, as for the *tzimtzum*: it is not *kipshuto*, and therefore the whole *gilui* of the *Atzmus* is in the *reshimu*, and that is no problem. You can have the *Kav* coming out of it: in the *koach hagvul* (the power of limit) you can still have the *gilui* of G-d as He is unlimited, as He transcends all forms.

blocks.question: Why talk about squirrels and trees, things of *Asiya*, when the subject is a high spiritual level before even *Atzilus*?
blocks.text:
What could acorns and squirrels and trees and furry rabbits have to do with it? This is supposed to be "cosmic energies of like the subconscious vibrations of supernal energies that vibrate in the inner core and essential quintessence of everything, something like that that nobody knows what it means." First of all, no. No.

Everything we talk about in the *hishtalshelus* (the chain of descent) is here in front of us. That is the point of learning the book: the *Atzmus Ein Sof* is here in front of us; G-d Himself is sitting here with us and we are staring Him in the face and do not know it. Not only that: we are actually getting a full *gilui* of the *Atzmus Ein Sof* before the *tzimtzum*, and the question is why we do not realize it. The book explains the whole process, but at the end we want to see it all back here, where we are: where is the *Atzmus Ein Sof* in my coffee? That is what is called *hashgacha pratis* (Divine providence): when you see these things in your coffee, not cosmic energies.

blocks.text: Now, what the student says is true: the *Kav* and the *reshimu* are things before the world was created. The *Kav* and *reshimu* are not the particular example he gives, but that does not mean the example does not actually come from them. Take how languages work: first you have a concept, then a symbolism, a representation, letters. You will say that the concept of letters exists before you get to the ABCs, and especially before ink on paper, the physical shapes. Yes, you are right: there is the concept of a letter. But when it comes all the way down the *hishtalshelus*, this *alef* on my paper is a letter. So the *reshimu* is G-d's ability to reveal a particular form.
blocks.outOfPlace: From the Q and A tape on chapter 15 (class 47), which reads no line: a student's question on class 40's squirrels and trees, answered with the reshimu of line 4.

blocks.text:
G-d is *kol yachol*, He can do whatever He wants, so He can assume any form He wants; if He wants to be a butterfly, He can be a butterfly. Before the *tzimtzum* we realize that He is choosing to do it, so you see the whole *Atzmus* in whatever He chooses to be, and to Him it is all the same. The *reshimu* is that G-d hides Himself and reveals all the options as if they were something separate from Him. That is the *reshimu* before it comes to any particular thing.

But everything from the *reshimu* down comes through the *reshimu*, so everything has a *reshimu*-ness to it: an aspect that is the source of the *keilim* (vessels), the source of its seeming a separate, limited, defined thing. When we look at something and see it as just a point, its own distinct entity, that is the *reshimu*. So when he gives an example from *Asiya*, that is actually the idea of the *reshimu*.

blocks.text: Another thing: when the Mitteler Rebbe goes through the *meshalim* (analogies) for the *reshimu*, he gives five, and only one of them is a *mashal* for the *reshimu*. The other four, as the Rebbe Rashab explains in *Ayin Beis*, are *meshalim* for how the *reshimu* is revealed in *ABYA*: the way the *reshimu* is seen in *Asiya*, the way it is seen in *Yetzira*. Throwing a stone is the *mashal* for the *reshimu*. The other four, the *Mishna* to the *Gemara*, the blueprint, the mnemonic and the hand motion, correspond to the way the *reshimu* is revealed in each of those worlds. The general *inyan* (concept) of the *reshimu* is that something looks separate and distant from G-d, as if He were no longer involved in it: maybe it came from Him, but now it is separate.

blocks.text: The squirrel is not the *reshimu* part of it. That you see existence, anything, as separate and distant from G-d, that it appears thrown: that is the *reshimu* of it. The essential nature of reality is that it appears separate, and you do not need a squirrel for that; a squirrel is just a thing in it. The *reshimu* is the *gilui* of G-d's power of *gvul* (limit), seen as separate from His power of *b'li gvul*, and that is where things seem thrown, separate.

blocks.question: And the teacher teaching a student: where is the *reshimu* there?
blocks.text:
That is the teacher's ability to make his information into *osios*, as if it were separate from him, as if the knowledge were going out separate from his mind. In different philosophies of how ideas work, ideas do not really exist outside of your mind, but we make them as if they do, and that is the idea of *osios*. Being put into *osios* like that is like his memory, and that is the *reshimu*. He has a power of memory, to keep ideas like letters stored in his brain without consciously thinking about them, as if they were their own existence that you can file away. Really you have to be thinking about everything all the time to keep it in your mind, but in a hidden way, so you do not see it; otherwise you would really forget it.

To make a *tzimtzum* and leave a *reshimu* is to clear your mind, put everything into your memory and leave your conscious mind blank: the *chalal reikan* and *makom panui*. Now you have a *makom panui* in your mind, and you can bring up the *osios* by way of a *Kav*, to bring them out to the student.

blocks.text: G-d wanted the world to look separate, so that we should have to work to see Him. So how is G-d revealed? You do not see Him so much in the thing itself. You see Him in the *Kav*, the changes He makes, in His *bechira*. That is what this chapter mainly explains: all the changes in the *hishtalshelus* are controlled only by G-d, and nothing else can make them. Like the body: it needs the soul to tell it what to do, and the *bechira* comes directly down through the whole *hishtalshelus*, from the top to the bottom, until it controls your little pinky toe. It all comes from you, and everything in the middle changes nothing. There you see the *inyan* of the *Kav*.

blocks.title: Brain, nerves and the moving object
blocks.text: *Tanya* spoke recently about the *Kav*, the *haara* (glow) of the *Kav*, and the *haara* of the *haara* of the *Kav*. Your essential *bechira* really goes only into your brain, your consciousness. From there it goes through your nerves into your organs and moves them according to your choice. If, G-d forbid, the connection of the nerves were cut somewhere, the person would make a choice and the body would not respond. Then the body, say your arm told to throw or move something, puts it into the thing. So when you see the thing moving, though the object is separate, you are seeing the effect of the body moving from the impulse of the nerves, from the choice he made in his brain.

blocks.text: So the actual light of the *Kav* is only in the brain. The *haara* of the *Kav* goes in the nerves to the body, and the body is like the *keilim* of *Atzilus*, still connected to the *Kav* because it is all connected through the nerves to the brain. When you write something, say something or make something, that is only a *haara* of the light of the *Kav*, of your choice; but it is a *bekia* (breaking through) of the *masach* (screen), and you can see the person in what he does. So we see G-d in that He controls everything and chooses how it should be. In the things themselves we do not see Him; they seem limited. We see Him in action.

blocks.text: Just as a soul fills the body, so G-d fills the world. That is the *inyan* of the *Midrash* on *Barchi nafshi es Hashem*: as the soul goes into the body and controls it, so G-d reveals Himself only through the *Kav*. It is one of the *meshalim* given for the *tzimtzum*, the soul controlling the body: the *etzem* of the soul stays out, higher than the body, yet it comes down and is connected to it, and so you see the soul in the body. That is the *inyan* that there is a *tzimtzum*, but not *kipshuto*: you see that there is *hashgacha*, that choices are going on, that G-d is changing things.

phrases.he: אינו בחינת צמצום גמור
phrases.en: it's not a complete *tzimtzum*, that G-d is preventing us from seeing Him.

phrases.en: That's because it's in a way of *koach hiyuli*.

blocks.text: **But there's another problem: the reshimu is in a way that it's not mispashet.** It is not only that everything was stuffed in there; it was stuffed in so short that there is no *hispashtus*. It is just like a point, so you have no way to start pulling the G-dliness out of it. The *Mishna* is different: it is still talking about the same thing as the *Gemara*, so you have something to work with, to figure out that it represents more than what is there, a little that contains a lot.

blocks.title: The rock and the bad guy's pit
blocks.text: But if G-d would just create this rock and have it floating there, never changing, just sitting there, and you came along and saw it, you would never figure out that there is any higher reality. You would be stuck. It is like those video games where you have to jump across these things, and after you are on them for a second they fall, and he keeps jumping across. You always wonder: why did the bad guy make it so that you can get across? He could just make one of these big pits without those things, and you would be stuck. That is what it would be like if there were only the *reshimu*: G-d would just stick us here in the world and we would be stuck, with no way of getting anywhere, because we would have nothing to work with. We would just have this rock; all we know is the rock. That is the *inyan* of the *reshimu*.

So the question is: how can we ever be expected to find G-d, if the way He makes the world is a *reshimu*, where it looks totally thrown and separate, just this thing with no apparent meaning? It is an absence of spreading downward. Even that: **it's not a complete tzimtzum, that G-d is preventing us from seeing Him**.

The only reason there is no inherent *gilui* in the physical world, or in anything in the *hishtalshelus*, so that each thing looked at in isolation lets you draw no conclusions and just is what it is, the *reshimu* of it, is **because it's in a way of koach hiyuli**: it really has the power to reveal G-d's whole *etzem*, and therefore you could make anything out of it. So until you can compare it to something else you have no reference, and you can't make anything out of it.

blocks.title: One word on a piece of paper
blocks.text: A person isolated in the world could figure out all kinds of possible explanations of reality; there would seem to be no inherent meaning, no clue to the meaning, if you look at things on their own. Like a language: how are you ever supposed to figure out what *Michal* means, those letters on the paper? Give a person a piece of paper with one word on it in a different language and tell him to figure out what it means; he will never figure it out. Why? Because letters inherently could mean anything. It is not that the letters stop you from knowing the meaning; it is because they are *hiyuli*, they could mean anything. The same letters could mean something else.

So too, the same creations G-d is making He could use to reveal anything. That He set it up so that certain things reveal certain aspects of Him, and other things other *middos* (attributes), He set up afterwards; that is already from the *Kav*. That a person can look at the world and you cannot force him to admit anything is there, is because there is a level of reality that is just an essential existence, separate from everything, and you could attach anything to it.

blocks.title: Ink on paper
blocks.text: You cannot prove to me from the ink that *v'hanimshal* should be read the way it is. You cannot prove that the *vav* should be read *vav* from the ink on the paper, if you look only at the ink, isolated from anything else. There is no way to prove anything, because it does not have to be anything: not that sound, not any sound. All it is is ink on paper. You cannot draw any other conclusions: it is ink in this shape, that is what it is. Anything else you want to tell me about it is not there; it is something you are associating with it. Those associations are a whole other layer of reality.

So that you do not inherently see it there is not because it stops you from making a language and associations; it is because it is the essential building block, and you can make anything out of it. So it is with the world: G-d first created all these isolated things, and then put them together in a certain order, in a certain form, that still works like a language, that reveals things. Or your body: it is set up in a certain way so that it reveals your soul, and works together in a certain way, but it did not have to be that way, in that form. If you just had a calcium molecule, why do you not see a person there? Because a calcium molecule does not have to be a person; it can maybe become part of anything. It is a whole other thing.

phrases.he: רק להיותו כח מגביל לכללות האור הראשון,
phrases.en: since the *reshimu* is this *koach* that limits the whole original light,

phrases.he: על כן בלתי מתפשט רק דרך קו, לפי אופן ההשפעה כנזכר לעיל.
phrases.en: Everything only comes out by way of a *Kav* according to the way that he wants to bring out the *hashpa'a*.

blocks.text: **Since the reshimu is this koach that limits the whole original light**, it is all there, G-d's whole *etzem* is there, and that means that every single thing has this quality: it just is, because it is. That is the root of the feeling of the *yesh gamur* (the complete, independent something). You know the saying that the *yesh gamur* comes from the *yesh amiti* (the true Existence)? This is what it means: the feeling of a *reshimu* is a *gilui* of the *Atzmus*. That something can be its own *metzius* (existence), with no cause and no purpose, that it is and always was and always will be, not for anything else, with no meaning, its own entity existing independently of everything else and needing nothing else: that is a *gilui* of G-d's *etzem*, a thing of G-d. Since G-d put Himself into every single thing, the whole light of the *etzem* is hidden there, and that is why you feel it, why you see it as the most basic, essential level of everything.
Therefore it is only revealed when you make a *Kav* out of it. For it to start revealing different things, you have to put an order on it, because essentially it could be in any order.

blocks.question: The *reshimu* is a bunch of *osios*, each with the whole *etzem*: is it one thing?
blocks.text: No, the *reshimu* is infinite. In this case it is the idea of something separate, but it is infinite. It is a zero of the *Ein Sof*, a zero compared to before the *tzimtzum*: like nothing, a single point, less than a single point. But that is compared to before. It is a zero of the *Atzmus* or *Ein Sof*, but it is infinite when it comes to *osios*, because the *reshimu*, it says, is all the *osios* of the *hashara*, the *gelaf glifu* (the engraving), just without the light: infinite *osios*. The *reshimu* is basically everything G-d is not, everything that does not look like G-d. G-d revealed to Himself, really, everything that does not look like Him.

blocks.title: The teacher's lesson order
blocks.text: Only some of them come out: the *Kav* brings out only some of the things from the *reshimu*, like the teacher who brings out only some of the explanations. **Everything only comes out by way of a Kav according to the way that he wants to bring out the hashpa'a** (the flow, the teaching): he has to choose to impose a *Kav* on it. From the teacher's side there is no *maala u'mata* (higher and lower) in his understanding; to him it is all equal, all the same. So he has to create a system and an order: you start here, then you do that, and then this.

That is what it says about this book. It says that *Chassidus* is *igulim* (circles): there is no *maala u'mata*, it is all one point, all the same level. You cannot say this is more basic and this more advanced, this is based on that; it is not true. Everything is its own thing that exists without everything else, and they are all really one point. Nevertheless it has to be learned in an orderly way, and the first thing is to know the *seder hishtalshelus* as it is explained in *Shaar HaYichud*. This *Shaar HaYichud* is a *Kav*: the Rebbeim made a *Kav* of how you should learn it. But this *Kav* is imposed, and when you start to understand it properly you see how it is all really the same, with the same essential point in it, everything just expressing it in a little different way.

sections.title: The Kav carries the infinite light, measured out for the receivers
sections.summary: The *Kav* has in it the light from before the *tzimtzum*, truly infinite, measured out only for the receivers, as a real teacher can explain anything at the student's level. Its order of higher and lower is a help to see G-d, the one who uses wisdom, and then to see His whole *etzem* in every point.

phrases.he: אמנם יובן מהנזכר לעיל דקו זה יש בו מכח האור הראשון שלפני הצמצום
phrases.en: However, from what we said in the last chapter, it's understood that really the *Kav* is not limited.

phrases.he: בבחינת אין סוף ממש,
phrases.en: It could bring out the whole light of before the *tzimtzum*, in a completely infinite way.

phrases.he: רק שבא דרך קו, לפי אופן המקבלים כו'
phrases.en: Just it's coming in a measured way according to the recipients.

blocks.text: **However, from what we said in the last chapter, it's understood that really the Kav is not limited.** **It could bring out the whole light of before the tzimtzum, in a completely infinite way.** The *Kav* is like the teacher who decides to explain in a measured way: but if he measures that the student is on his level, he can bring it all the way back out to his own level, his teacher's level. **Just it's coming in a measured way according to the recipients**: if they are little, it comes in a little way, and he can explain anything from his knowledge.

When the Mitteler Rebbe gives a *mashal* of a teacher and a student who are *b'erech* (in proportion), he means a real teacher, and a real teacher has the essence of intellect. "Then this is an exaggeration, like almost nobody really has the essence of intellect." The essence of intellect is really *Chassidus*, and then you really know everything; it is only a matter of putting it together in different ways. You see the essence of it. It is not that you learned a whole bunch of things; it is a qualitatively different type of understanding. "But we don't have time to get into explaining that now."

blocks.title: The posek hador
blocks.text: He really knows everything and could explain anything to you, but he tells you what you can know. You can understand it even on a basic level. Someone has really mastered *halacha*, say he is the *posek hador* (the halachic authority of the generation), and you come and ask him a question. He knows *halacha* with *omek* (depth), so whatever situation you come up with, he did not have to learn about that situation; he will figure out how to put the pieces together and tell you the *halacha* for it. But he has to measure what situation you are talking about, and put it together accordingly. Yet if you are on the right level, he can go all the way back up and talk to you on his level, where he sees everything.

So what does this mean? Within the *Kav* G-d could reveal His whole *etzem*, but He chose to make the *hishtalshelus*. Since He wants to make limited things, He reveals Himself only in a limited way, so each thing seems to have its own *chayus* (life force), its own *gilui* of G-dliness unique to it, and it all seems to be a limited system. G-d created that so that we could have *avoda* (divine service) and have the world. But if He wanted, He could blow it back up and show how you really have the whole *koach* of the *Ein Sof* in you, or in my coffee, or whatever it is.

phrases.he: ובזה יובן מה שכתוב באורך נראה אור
phrases.en: from Your light we see a different light,

phrases.he: בחינת הארה דהארה
phrases.en: only like a ray of a ray,

phrases.he: הנקרא אור של תולדה
phrases.en: which is called like a born light, meaning that it changes its form.

phrases.he: שאחר הצמצום בוקע האור דרך קו בעלמא כו',
phrases.en: after the *tzimtzum*, the light breaks through, … but it's only coming through the *Kav*.

phrases.he: אבל הוא בא מאורך העצמי
phrases.en: but the light that we're seeing is coming from Your essential light.

phrases.he: להיות שברשימו הרי נכלל הכל
phrases.en: because the whole *etzem* is really hidden in the *reshimu*,

phrases.he: וממנו נמשך הקו
phrases.en: and the *Kav* is coming out from the *reshimu*,

blocks.text: And with this we understand what is written, **from Your light we see a different light**: **only like a ray of a ray**, **which is called like a born light, meaning that it changes its form**: the *or shel tolda*. The light we are seeing is G-d's light, which means we are seeing G-d Himself. But G-d made it a light of a light that changes, so to us it looks like a revelation of something else, of *chachma* (wisdom) or *Keser* (crown) or *bina*. Then these come into more particular things: it looks like the wisdom of squirrels, a particular life force or *chayus*, a particular truth. In that we see a little reflection of the G-dly spark, a little reflection of G-d, but not the whole picture. We just feel that there is a little something in it, behind it, and through it we can get a glimpse of the Creator who made it.

**After the tzimtzum, the light breaks through**: the original light, so that you see a little glimmer of G-d, **but it's only coming through the Kav**, only in this limited, measured way. The vessel of wisdom, the concept of wisdom as something separate from G-d, comes from the *reshimu*: G-d is not wisdom. But you see that there is someone using the wisdom, executing it in the world, and that is a *bekia* of the *Atzmus Or Ein Sof*: you see that G-d Himself is the one doing the wisdom.

blocks.title: Smarter than an apple tree
blocks.text: The trees and the squirrels, anything: you see wisdom, a big wisdom. "I mean I don't know about you, but like I don't know how to make apples, and between you and me, I think I'm smarter than an apple tree, so I don't think the apple tree knows how to make an apple either, cause it's just stupid wood." It is G-d's wisdom telling it how to do it. Or spiders making their webs: they do not know how to make a web; it is not that they are smart guys who figured it out. G-d put it into them. Or bees: they make honeycombs at perfect angles, whatever degree you need; it is genetic, they know how to do it, and they are not that smart. You see that there is a wise guy behind it, someone higher than wisdom who is using the wisdom.

blocks.title: Hearing a person in the sounds
blocks.text: Right now, talking to you, I hear intelligence in the sounds you are making, so I do not just say, oh, there is intelligence. I say there is a person who is intelligent. I see you only through your intelligence and the other ways you express yourself, but I am seeing you; I do not think you are this intelligence. It is a quality you have, not your *etzem*. So too, we can realize that there is a G-d, that He is the one who uses wisdom, and that He is higher than wisdom; you cannot say that G-d is wisdom. But now it comes only through the ten *sefiros* (the Divine attributes), which are the *Kav* that G-d measures out, so to see G-d we have to see Him through His wisdom, His will, His kindness and these things.

**But the light that we're seeing is coming from Your essential light.** We are really seeing G-d Himself: though it comes now through the limited form, it really reveals the original light, **because the whole etzem is really hidden in the reshimu**, **and the Kav is coming out from the reshimu**.

phrases.he: בבחינת היולי לכללות השפע להיות בבחינת מעלה ומטה
phrases.en: The *Kav* is a *hiyuli* to make things in a way of *maala u'mata*.

phrases.he: על כל פנים,
כמו שכתוב בעץ חיים
phrases.en: like it says in *Etz Chaim*.

blocks.text: The *Kav* reveals what is hidden in the *reshimu* only in a way of *maala u'mata*, so that you have a way to start. It makes a progression: you start with A, then do B, and slowly work your way to seeing G-d. But once the *Kav* helps you *chap* (grasp) G-d, you see Him in the thing itself. Every point is *mamash* chosen by Him; He *mamash* put His *etzem* into that point, so you now see the whole *etzem* in every point. That it was made *maala u'mata* was only to help you come to that realization.

blocks.title: One letter and many letters
blocks.text: When a person writes in a language, he puts the *sechel* (intellect) into really every single letter. But for you to *chap* that there is a *sechel*, he has to make a lot of letters; it is easier to *chap* when there are a lot of letters.

The *etzem or* is revealed because it is hidden in the *reshimu*: the *reshimu* really has the whole *etzem or* in it. So really every point has the whole *etzem* in it, but you do not see it, because it is a *hiyuli*, and you do not know how to pull the *etzem or* out of it. So G-d reveals it in a *Kav*, only a limited *hamshacha* (drawing down) of it, a limited *gilui* in a way of *maala u'mata*. In a way that is not true: it is not that G-d insists it must be *davka* a certain way, that you have to start here and then go there. But once you go through that *Kav*, it reveals to you the *etzem* of the *reshimu*; it helps you find the *Atzmus* hidden in the *reshimu*. That is what he is saying: the *Kav* is drawn from the *reshimu*, and therefore you can see the light of the *Atzmus* that was put into it.

**The Kav is a hiyuli to make things in a way of maala u'mata.** The *reshimu* is a *hiyuli* for everything. As we explained in the last chapter, a measuring stick is a *hiyuli* to measure anything. *Al kol panim* (at any rate) it should already be *maala u'mata*: the only thing the *Kav* says is that it will be *maala u'mata*, but within that you can make any *maala u'mata* you want. There will be an order and a certain form, a starting point and an end point, so that you will have a way to *chap* what he is saying. You start here and end there, but you can do it however you want. Like explaining an idea in words: you can write whatever you want on the paper, but it has to start here and go from right to left; certain rules already make it *maala u'mata*, a certain order. **Like it says in Etz Chaim.**

sections.title: Two opposites in the Kav: it unites, and it measures
sections.summary: The *Kav* unites all the lights, so that even *chesed* can go into the vessel of *gevura*, and it is also the *kav hamida* that measures every light and vessel and makes the distinctions. That looks like a contradiction, but whoever makes the rules can break the rules.

phrases.he: ומזה הטעם
phrases.en: for this reason

phrases.he: יובן תירוץ על ב' ענינים הפכים שנמצא בקו זה
phrases.en: we can answer the seeming paradox of two things we see in this *Kav* that seem to be opposite things:

phrases.he: הא' אשר בכחו דוקא לאכללא שמאלא בימינא כו'
phrases.en: that the *Kav* can make *hiskalelus* between opposites,

phrases.he: שהוא בחינת ההתכללות והיחודים של כל האורות המסתעפים מכתר דאדם קדמון עד מלכות דאצילות
phrases.en: that the *Kav* is *davka* what makes everything work together.

phrases.he: עד שעל ידו דוקא יוחלף האור בכלי שאינו שלו,
phrases.en: until *davka* from the *Kav*, the light can go into its opposite vessel even,

phrases.he: כמו אור החסד בכלי הגבורה כו'
phrases.en: that you can decide that you're going to express your *chesed* through *gevura*.

phrases.he: כמו שכתוב במקום אחר באריכות בענין וא''ו דוהנורא כו'
phrases.en: like it explains at length in other places, about the *vav* of *v'hanora*

blocks.text: **For this reason** **we can answer the seeming paradox of two things we see in this Kav that seem to be opposite things.** The first: **that the Kav can make hiskalelus between opposites** (inclusion of one in the other): it can show you how two things that seem opposites work together and are really one thing. **The Kav is davka what makes everything work together**, all the lights from *Keser* of *Adam Kadmon* to *Malchus* (kingship) of *Atzilus*. It is like the *mashal* of a person: all the different *ratzonos* (wills) and powers, the power of *chachma* and the others, all work together so that you control them, and you see a uniting thing, a person using them. That is your choice, your conscious control of all those faculties and abilities.

**Until davka from the Kav, the light can go into its opposite vessel even**, like the light of *chesed* (kindness) in the vessel of *gevura* (might, restraint): **you can decide that you're going to express your chesed through gevura**. So you will be nice to the person through being mean or strict. "You're not a machine, you're not stuck." That is the point: you are not stuck in a certain system; you have free choice to do whatever you want.

**Like it explains at length in other places, about the vav of v'hanora.** In *Shemoneh Esreh* we say *hagadol, hagibor v'hanora*: *hagadol* is *chesed*, *hagibor* is *gevura*, and *hanora* is *tiferes*, the middle line. There you see the *vav*, the *Kav*: the *Kav* is what puts right and left together, what connects the *chesed* and *gevura*, and that is *v'hanora*, wondrous, which comes through the power of the *Kav*, the *vav*. There you see that the essence of the *vav* is the *etzem* thing that goes straight down through everything equally, that control. *Hagadol* means that He is infinite, transcendent; *hagibor*, that He can limit Himself to be revealed as a limited thing; and *hanora*, that He can put the two together and make the limited thing infinite and the infinite thing limited, until they are *mamash* one thing. That is the *Kav*: G-d is revealed as able to do whatever He wants and put things together however He wants.

phrases.he: והב'
phrases.en: and the second thing that we see in the *Kav*,

phrases.he: מה שנקרא בשם קו המדה דוקא,
phrases.en: it's called the measuring line

phrases.he: למדוד כל אורות וכלים כו'
phrases.en: to measure all lights and vessels, to set their limits

phrases.he: וכנזכר לעיל בענין הקו
שנקרא אמת הבנין כו'
phrases.en: it's called like the measuring rod

phrases.he: שזהו היפוך ההתכללות לכאורה.
phrases.en: which is the opposite of *hiskalelus* seemingly,

blocks.text: **And the second thing that we see in the Kav**: **it's called the measuring line**, the *kav hamida*, **to measure all lights and vessels, to set their limits**: how far they go, what will be the definition of *chachma* and of *bina*, where their boundaries will be, here is *chachma* and here is *bina*; to make the distinctions. As was said of the *Kav*, **it's called like the measuring rod**. **Which is the opposite of hiskalelus seemingly**: it is the ability to create distinctions and a system. Really it is making false distinctions; that is the real thing of the *Kav*, since the teacher sees it all as one thing.

blocks.title: Addition and subtraction as separate subjects
blocks.text: For the benefit of the student the teacher creates these kind of false distinctions and systems, as if addition were different from subtraction, with nothing to do with it, a separate subject. He does it to make it simple: you start with this. But to him it is really not like that. So seemingly the whole thing of the *Kav* is to make differentiation.

And the obvious answer is *hainu hach* (this is that): "If you make the rules, you can break the rules, it's synonymous." To say that I have the ability to make whatever rules I want also means that I can break the rules, as we were saying about law: that you decide how to interpret the law really means there is no law, you are always doing whatever you want. So setting rules and breaking rules is really just you doing what you want; it looks like two different things, but it is the same thing. That is the *Kav*: sometimes G-d wants us to make rules, sometimes He wants to break rules.

sections.title: Both are true: the Atzmus in the Kav unites, the reshimu in it measures
sections.summary: Because the *Kav* comes from the *Atzmus* before the *tzimtzum*, it can unite every opposite, and for the very same reason it can measure every light, vessel and union: unlimited means able to be as limited as He wants. The *reshimu* in it is the blueprint that makes the world look set, with a *teva*, so that there can be *avoda*.

phrases.he: אך הענין הוא דשניהם אמת
phrases.en: the *inyan* is that they're both true.

phrases.he: ואדרבה
phrases.en: and not only they're both true, on the contrary,

phrases.he: הא בהא תליא
phrases.en: they're interdependent, it's *mamash* one thing,

phrases.he: משום דשרש זה הקו מכח הראשון דעצמיות אור אין סוף שלפני הצמצום הוא בא
phrases.en: So since this *Kav* comes from the *koach* of the *atzmiyus Ein Sof* before the *tzimtzum*,

phrases.he: כנזכר לעיל בענין באורך דוקא נראה אור דקו זה
phrases.en: like we said that it's *davka* from G-d's light that we're seeing the light,

blocks.text: **The inyan is that they're both true.** **And not only they're both true, on the contrary**, **they're interdependent, it's mamash one thing**. **Since this Kav comes from the koach of the atzmiyus Ein Sof before the tzimtzum**: G-d is unlimited, He can do whatever He wants, there are no limitations. As was said earlier, **it's davka from G-d's light that we're seeing the light**, the cause of the *Kav*: He is really revealing Himself, so there are really no limitations and He can do whatever He wants.

phrases.he: ובכח האור העצמות דאין סוף ודאי יש לעשות בחינת התכללות ויחודים של כל ההפכים בכל ההשתלשלות מראש דאדם קדמון כו'
phrases.en: surely the *Atzmus Ein Sof* can connect and unite everything in the whole *hishtalshelus*, it's all one thing.

phrases.he: עד מלכות דאצילות
וכמאמר אנת הוא דמייחד לון ומקשר לון כו',
phrases.en: like it says that You are the one that unites them and ties them together and connects them,

phrases.he: אנת הוא מלגאו ומלבר כו'
phrases.en: You are on the inside and the outside,

phrases.he: וכן ענין שם מ''ה מלגאו דאיהו אורח כל האצילות כו'
phrases.en: this is the *inyan* of the Name *MaH* that's on the *pnimiyus* of the *sefiros*, which is the path that unites *Atzilus*, that is the *Kav*.

phrases.he: וכהאי גוונא
הכל הוא מצד הארת אור העצמות דאין סוף שבקו זה,
phrases.en: that's because the *Kav* is shining with the *or* of the *Atzmus d'Ein Sof*,

blocks.text: **Surely the Atzmus Ein Sof can connect and unite everything in the whole hishtalshelus, it's all one thing.** It is the essence of everything, so it transcends all the differences and can bring them all together, make them all get along. So surely it can connect everything, since it is coming from the *Atzmus Ein Sof*.

**Like it says that You are the one that unites them and ties them together and connects them**, **You are on the inside and the outside**: to You the *pnimiyus* (inner side) and *chitzoniyus* (outer side) are the same. There is no inside and outside, it is all the same, You unite everything. *Davka* G-d's *etzem*, *Ant* (You): *davka* You can unite everything, because You transcend all limitations.

**This is the inyan of the Name MaH that's on the pnimiyus of the sefiros, which is the path that unites Atzilus, that is the Kav.** The *Kav* is the inner *MaH*, the inner *bittul* (self-nullification), the soul of *Atzilus* as it were: G-d's choice, the way He consciously controls and chooses how everything should be. That is the *inyan* of the *Kav*.

**That's because the Kav is shining with the or of the Atzmus d'Ein Sof**, **all the way down to Malchus, the lowest levels**. The light of the *Atzmus Or Ein Sof* can shine all the way down there and reveal that it is really not limited, that it is really G-d Himself, and break all the limitations.

phrases.en: yet this itself is the reason

phrases.he: שיש בכחו למדוד מדה וגבול לכל אורות וכלים
phrases.en: why He's able to limit and measure everything, set a limitation for everything, in all the lights and vessels,

phrases.en: however He decided in *Atzmus Ein Sof* before the *tzimtzum*.

blocks.text: **Yet this itself is the reason** **why He's able to limit and measure everything, set a limitation for everything, in all the lights and vessels**: **in every union between a mashpia and mekabel** (giver and receiver) **it should be davka a certain way**, **how much the mashpia is going to come to the mekabel and how much the mekabel is going to have to come up to the mashpia**. That is the idea of *MaD and MaN*, *mayin duchrin* and *mayin nukvin* (the male and female waters).

**Because of the reshimu which limits the light of the Atzmus in different ways.** Even the *reshimu* is the power to limit the light of the *Atzmus* in infinite ways, any possible way He wants. And since the *Kav* is basically G-d choosing which combination to make between the transcendent *gilui* of the *Atzmus Ein Sof* and the limited *gilui* of the *reshimu*, it is the same thing: if you say He can choose to make it as bright as He wants, it means He can make it as dark as He wants. As unlimited or as limited as He wants: He can do whatever He wants, **however He decided in Atzmus Ein Sof before the tzimtzum**.

Those limitations come from the *reshimu*, because it is the *gilui* of the *Or Ein Sof* through the *reshimu*: the *reshimu* is all the different ways G-d can reveal His light. Like the teacher with all the different explanations in his head: the explanations are like the *reshimu*, and his knowledge, which transcends all the explanations and unites them, is like the *Atzmus* of the light. When he measures it out for the students, he picks which explanations to use and sets up a structure to limit it. In a way that is superficial, because he sees how it is all connected, and he also sees how it could be divided up in all different ways. He picks the way he thinks most appropriate for the student and explains it, and as they go up the ladder maybe he shows them that it is really more connected than he made it look, and not so simple.

blocks.title: The Bohr model
blocks.text: When you learn things at a lower level, they try to make things really simple. When they teach you about the atom and the electron, they teach you the Bohr model, with the little balls spinning around. When you get more advanced, they tell you it is really nothing like that at all; that is way too simple. It is really not that divided, you cannot point to where the electron is at all, it is barely even a thing, just this energy field. The real *etzem* of the way they understand it is not a system. But to make it simple, they put this whole system and explanation on it, and it is totally not like that.

blocks.title: Negative numbers
blocks.text: Really any concept is not a system, like math. They make arithmetic into addition and subtraction, but you do not really have to separate addition and subtraction as if they were two opposite or different things. As soon as you start adding negative numbers, they are the same thing.

phrases.en: So it comes out, when we look at the *Kav*, there's two sides you can look at it. From the side of the *Atzmus* of the *or* that's in it, it's a *hiyuli* thing to unite everything.

blocks.text: **So it comes out, when we look at the Kav, there's two sides you can look at it.** **From the side of the Atzmus of the or that's in it, it's a hiyuli thing to unite everything**: it has this essential ability to unite everything. **But because it's coming from the reshimu**, it is able **to give a limit, and it's able to impose this artificial limitation and order onto everything**, according to **however He decided in the reshimu how He was going to do it**.

blocks.title: The architect's blueprint
blocks.text: **Like a mashal of a craftsman, like an architect**: **he makes a blueprint for how to make whatever it is**, say a house; but it could be a chair, or an *aron kodesh* (a holy ark), or a silver *kiddush* cup. First they draw out the plan of how to make it, and then they make it. Now that he is actually making it, he has his blueprint, with a little key at the bottom that says an inch on the paper means a foot, or ten feet. Then he has his measuring stick and he measures it out and builds it: that is what you need, a measuring rod, to measure one inch and then ten feet and follow the blueprint for the house. **So now he has this blueprint in order that everything should be built exactly the way that he decided.**

The main thing of the *reshimu* is that **he doesn't want to deviate from his original plan**: he makes a blueprint so that it is all set and he does not have to rethink it; it is there. In the *nimshal*, it makes the world look set, as if it is a certain way and cannot be a different way: it makes it look like it has a *teva* (nature).

blocks.title: Name and date in the corner
blocks.text: That gives us the ability of *avoda*. In a classroom, or any kind of education, if you want to put the burden of effort on the students, the class has to have a strict system they must conform to: they have to do their homework in a certain way and answer the tests in a certain way, and if they do not write their name and the date and use a certain format, you will not give them credit. Really you do not have to do that. Some teachers are much looser: "Yeah, you know, I see you tried making effort and you understand, and I'm going to give you credit." But especially for younger, immature kids, if you want to make them work, and to feel they are accomplishing things, it has to be demanding, and it is only demanding if you say it has to be a certain way.

blocks.title: You're the teacher, man
blocks.text: You do not really care whether they write their name in this corner and the date in that corner and use a certain format; you just kind of invent the format, and then you make it as if that is the rule: it has to be done that way, or else it is no good. "What do you mean? You're the teacher, man. What do you mean, where do you get this magical rule that things have to be that way?" But he makes it as if it were outside his control: it has to be that way.

sections.title: Every change comes from the Atzmus: the teacher who leaves his plan
sections.summary: When the light comes beyond the measure of the *Kav*, or less than it, that is only from the *Atzmus*, the one who made the plan and can change it, as only the husband can change the blueprint of the house. Every change in the worlds, from *Shabbos* to *galus*, comes from there, and so we pray to His very *Atzmus* to change even the simple will.

phrases.he: ואף על פי שאם לפעמים יהיה תוספת אור בנאצלים, יתר מכפי מאמר קו המדה כו',
phrases.en: but sometimes G-d breaks the rules, and He makes more of a *gilui* than the way He says it's supposed to be.

phrases.he: היינו מכח האור העצמות דוקא
phrases.en: Has to be *davka* from the *koach haAtzmus*, that He can make it more,

phrases.he: שלפעמים יאיר כך ולפעמים יאיר כך
phrases.en: Sometimes He does it this way, sometimes He does it that way.

blocks.text: So you say, wait a minute: **but sometimes G-d breaks the rules, and He makes more of a gilui than the way He says it's supposed to be**. He said that for there to be a *gilui* you have to do the *avoda*, and sometimes you just get inspired and you did not work. "Sometimes G-d gives you a freebie." Sometimes G-d inspires people, or shows them *hashgacha pratis* or a miracle, and they did not work for it.

So what happened to the whole thing that we have to do *avoda*? The main thing of the *kav hamida* in *avoda* is, as it says in *HaYom Yom*, that with the three kinds of *hisbonenus* (contemplation) it is impossible to get a *gilui Elokus* (a revelation of G-dliness) without doing all three steps in order. You cannot jump, you cannot skip steps. Sometimes, he says, G-d will give you a little *gilui milmaala* (a revelation from above), but that is a special thing; normally you have to go through all these steps or it will not work, and you will not get *Elokus* any other way. That is the *Kav*: G-d sets it up so that you have to go through every single step of the *hishtalshelus*, or else it will not work. And you have to be *misbonen* on each one, as we explained in chapter one: first the *bina*, the length and the width and the depth, and then you have to get the *chachma* and the *Keser*. It is a whole *avoda*.

And then sometimes G-d gives them freebies and they get this inspirational thing; it says that it does not last, it is not *b'pnimiyus* (inward), but sometimes G-d makes more of a *gilui*. Sometimes the teacher breaks the rules and makes an exception for somebody. It **has to be davka from the koach haAtzmus, that He can make it more**.

blocks.title: The class trip to NASA
blocks.text: **Sometimes He does it this way, sometimes He does it that way.** It is as the listener was just saying, the *mashal* of the teacher. First he makes a class plan, which is like the *Kav*: first we do this, then we learn that, a whole program for each day, what they will do and in what order. But sometimes he goes outside the class plan and takes them on a trip, say to NASA. They are little kids learning science and they do not understand, but the point is that it gives them a wow: they realize there is something way above them, and it motivates them to want to work to go higher, and they realize that they could do it.

That is like *krias Yam Suf* (the splitting of the Sea): G-d gave them a *gilui* like *Moshe*'s *nevua* (prophecy), bigger than *Yechezkel*'s, way beyond their level. And at *Matan Torah* (the giving of the Torah) G-d gave them a big *gilui* way beyond their level, a taste of *Olam HaBa* (the World to Come); they were like *tzaddikim*. But that was only so that they would appreciate what they could eventually reach. Afterwards it went back to the plan and they had to start doing it on their own; it was to motivate them to want to get there, and to realize that there is much more, beyond the way they are learning it and doing it now.

blocks.title: Extra problems and a pop quiz
blocks.text: And then sometimes they are bad, and, as the listener said, he just tells them to sit there and gives them extra problems to do, or tells them to sit there and do nothing, or gives them a pop quiz. What happened to the plan, when we were supposed to learn more? That is the thing: because it is coming from the *etzem*, the teacher can decide whatever he wants.

There are two things here. First, he can decide to do what he wants, so he is not really stuck in the plan: he made the rules, he can break the rules. Second, you will say: what happened? Yesterday he was real nice, and today he became mean; so is the teacher nice or is he mean? We say no, he did not change; it is really the same *Kav*. He wants the students to learn and understand the subject. If he measures that the regular class is good for them, he gives them the regular class; if something special is better, he gives them something special; if a punishment is better, he gives them a punishment. It is really the same goal; he is only measuring it out according to the *mekablim* (receivers), what they need. "Oh, the teacher became mean." No, he did not become mean; it is the same thing.

phrases.he: ולזה הטעם כל בחינת התחדשות אור באבי''ע, הכל מעצמות אור אין סוף שלפני הצמצום דוקא
phrases.en: this is the reason why any new thing, any change at all in the light of *ABYA*, has to come from *Atzmus Or Ein Sof*, before *tzimtzum*, *davka*.

phrases.he: דהיינו מפני שבאורו העצמי נראה אור בקו זה
phrases.en: because the light that's coming on the *Kav* is coming from G-d's *etzem or*.

phrases.he: לפעמים בתוספת ולפעמים בגרעון
phrases.en: Sometimes it comes more, sometimes it comes less.

blocks.text: **This is the reason why any new thing, any change at all in the light of ABYA, has to come from Atzmus Or Ein Sof, before tzimtzum, davka**: that is the only one that has jurisdiction to change the *Kav*, to change the plan.

Once a teacher makes a class plan, if everything is running: "some teachers are like this, they're like these robots." They make a class plan and have to follow it; they make it as if they are totally stuck in the rules, they are not human, they cannot make an exception even when they are totally unreasonable, and they don't care. "Like, you could be dying, they don't care, they won't give you an exception." Because that is it, it is a system: once you set a system, you have to follow it. If you want to change it, you have to go to the *etzem*; it has to be a human thing.

That is because it is a system: once you set a system, you have to follow it. If you want to change it, you have to go to the *etzem*; it has to be a human thing.

blocks.text: So too with any change going on in the *hishtalshelus*, and really there are changes going on every single moment if you look at it, because it is not really a system. But certainly when it is something obvious, a miracle or anything, it has to be coming from the *Atzmus*; or a hurricane, or anything.

blocks.title: The architect builds the house himself
blocks.text: **Because the light that's coming on the Kav is coming from G-d's etzem or.** **Sometimes it comes more, sometimes it comes less.** Though it is measured out according to a system, it is really coming from the *Atzmus*; He is deciding. The architect himself is taking the blueprint and building the house. He made the blueprint, so if he wants he can say, "Well, I'm following this, and I don't care about anything else. This is the way it says, this is the way it's going to be. That's it, that's the plan, we have to do it." But if he wants, he can also say, "You know, I made the plan, I can change the plan," and make something bigger than it says, or smaller than it says. He can do what he wants.

The *asara maamaros* (the ten utterances of creation) are one way you see it. But even *b'etzem* (in itself): if you look carefully at the world, it looks like a system at first, but it is not. There is a level where it looks like a system, which covers over G-dliness, but when you look carefully, with chaos theory and things like that, to give just one example, you realize that it is really not a system. So you cannot say that it was just thrown; you must say that there is a conscious volition telling everything what to do every second, just as with the body.

blocks.title: A whole world inside of you
blocks.text: Look at the body under a microscope, and at first it is just a bunch of different cells, each one like its own organism: tree cells, squirrel cells, people cells, all just sitting there doing their own thing, trillions of little things living their own lives and running all over the place. The ones that move around, like the blood cells, are like animals; the ones that stay put but grow are like plants; and the ones that do not move at all, like bone cells or minerals, are like stones. It is *mamash* a whole world inside of you. Look at each one individually and it has its own *ratzon* and its own brain telling it what to do; it just tries to live its own life. It does not know there is a person, and does not care. But there is this will, a higher thing imposed on all of them, that makes them all work together. It is like a *makif* on them, and they do not even know it.
blocks.outOfPlace: From the second Q and A tape on chapter 15 (class 48), which reads no line: the world looks like a system, but a will above it makes every change, as lines 37 to 39 say.

blocks.text: It is the same with the world. Under a microscope, the molecules and atoms and quarks each look like their own little thing, following their own rules and system according to their *teva*. But there is a gap between the levels: at the atomic level they seem each to be doing their own thing, and they should not work together on the molecular level the way they do, or come together into a tree that works together. Going from one level to the next, scientifically the only way to explain it is some outside *makif* force that unites them, because nothing in the individuals does it. A left kidney cell does not have the full DNA, only kidney cell DNA. Each cell has its own brain, so to speak, and does not know the whole picture of what it is supposed to be doing; it knows only what it is supposed to do, and tries to do that the best it can.

blocks.title: The cancer cell
blocks.text: A cancer cell is when one of them somehow loses its *bittul*: the system that keeps the things working together breaks down, and a kidney cell tries to turn everything into kidney cells. It makes a bunch of kidney cells, but you do not need that many, and they are not the right shape; it is all wrong. It loses the *bittul* to the general thing.

blocks.title: What keeps the cells in order
blocks.text: What is doing that? They are not sure yet exactly what does it in the body. When they figure it out, *im yirtzeh Hashem* soon, and they are researching it, they should be able to cure cancer and to make people live forever; so hopefully they will figure it out soon. They are already researching, in embryology, what causes this *bittul* over the body when a child first starts to develop. A baby develops very rapidly, yet everything somehow develops in the right proportions, order and form, and they are not sure how it knows to do that. They know there are different chemicals there that influence it, mainly a liquid he thinks, but they have not yet isolated them and figured out what does what. And *l'mai nafka mina* (what difference does it make): it is the *tipa* (the drop), with *hei gevuros* and *hei chasadim*; some of the liquids make it grow and some make it stop, and the right combination of the five *gevuros* and five *chasadim* makes it come in the right form. Rabbi Walters knew from *Chassidus* that these liquids are there in the child and make it develop, before he researched it in medicine and realized that they were researching it.

blocks.title: Chassidus and the body
blocks.text: It also seems that some sort of inhalant would trigger the proper release of these chemicals in an adult, so that the body would start to fix itself up again. What happens as people get older is that this liquid dries up, the body loses the signals to fix itself up, and it starts to deteriorate. It does not have to come through scientific discovery; it could come from learning *Chassidus*. If you learn *Chassidus* properly, it will happen naturally, it will do this to your body. Learning *Chassidus* physically has a certain effect on your body; they will figure out independently, on a physical level, how it could be done, but to do it properly, *mamash* in its real form, the best form, it has to come *davka* through *Chassidus*.

blocks.title: The pool room
blocks.text: It is like a *mashal* of newlyweds building their house from scratch. The wife goes down one day to see what is going on: they have dug, poured the cement for the foundation and started putting up the frame. Someone gives her a tour and shows her the blueprint and what is going to be where: here the kitchen and the dining room, the living room and the bedrooms and the guest room, "and this is going to be the pool room," for shooting pool. "What? I don't want a pool room. Make it a guest room, or make the kitchen bigger. I need a bigger kitchen. That's too small. I need to have a *milchig*, *fleishig* and a *pareve* island, and a *Pesach* kitchen." He says, "Well, I can't do that. I'm just the contractor, you have to go to the boss." So she goes to the boss, and he says, "I can't. You have to go to the architect and engineer, I can't change the blueprint."

blocks.title: Sorry lady, go to your husband
blocks.text: The architect says, "Sorry lady, you got to go to your husband. We agreed to this, and it was based on what he wanted. I just drew up the plans; I didn't invent it." He knows what is structurally sound, but what is going to be where, "I didn't decide that." Then she goes to her husband: "I don't want a pool room." "What? Honey, I want a pool room, why not? So much fun." "No. I want a *Pesach* kitchen, or a bigger kitchen, or a guest room." "Oh, okay." And he tells them to change it, and everything changes.

blocks.text: So we see from this *mashal* that if you want to change anything in the *hishtalshelus*, even the smallest little *prat* (detail) all the way down in *Asiya*, you have to go all the way up to G-d, because nothing in the *hishtalshelus* has the jurisdiction to make any change. It is like a phone: its whole purpose is to give over what you are saying without changing it (though we have phones with static). G-d set up the *hishtalshelus* perfectly; it cannot put in any input of its own and change it; it just faithfully gives over what G-d wants. So if you want to change something, each level says, "Well, you have to go to my boss." You go to the *Keser*, which comes from the *Malchus* of the upper world, and you keep going up until you get to the *ratzon kadum* (the preceding will), and it says, "Well, I come from the *Kav*." You go to the *Kav*, and it says, "I'm just the *hiyuli*. I don't have any *pratim*, you have to go to G-d; He's the one that measures things out for me." Then you go to G-d, and He says, "Oh."

blocks.text: And with the husband, his real *ratzon* is not this way or that; he just wants him and his wife to be happy. He thought the pool room would make her happy, but if she says she would rather have it a different way, he will make it a different way. So he did not change his *ratzon*; the *etzem* stays the same, and he just measures it out differently. So too with us, when we *daven* (pray), or think of *bitachon* (trust), whenever we ask G-d for a change: G-d can make the world different and still accomplish the same goal. He can just measure it out differently; to Him it is the same, it does not matter, because we asked Him for this.

That is what it says: we say in *davening* on *Shabbos* that G-d made the world according to His *ratzon*, the *ratzon* of the *tzaddikim* and the *ratzon* of all the Jews. "It was your fault." You planned it out with Him and picked what part you were going to have in the world: your life, your goal and your challenges. Then you come down here and start complaining, and He says, "What do you mean? I thought that's what you said you wanted." You wanted the challenges; that is the main thing you wanted, and you cannot complain now.

That is the thing, though: to change it, you have to reveal all the way back to the *etzem* in yourself. As long as you are dealing with the lower levels you can whine, but even within yourself that does not mean you really want it to be different. You have to be aware of what is really going on, to really know whether you want it different; then you can ask, and G-d will change it for you.

So too **the changes in all the faces from Adam Kadmon all the way down to the heel of Adam Kadmon, all the way in Asiya**. That is like the teacher: sometimes he shows a nice face, and sometimes a strict face, a mean face, and he punishes. So it is all the way through the whole *hishtalshelus*, whether G-d shows it in a big *gilui* or not.

blocks.title: The field trip and the homework
blocks.text: Like the change from the time of the *Beis HaMikdash* (the Temple) to the time of *galus* (exile). The time of the *Beis HaMikdash* is like the teacher saying, okay, now we are going on a field trip, and rewarding them. The time of *galus* is like his saying, just sit and do nothing, or sit and do homework: make them sweat a little. If they do not want to do the *yegia* (toil) on their own to learn, it refines them to make them do *yegia*, even if it is on nothing really. That is *galus*: we have to do much more *yegia*, much more raising of *MaN*, to get any little *MaD*, and G-d does not give us any freebies as far as *gilui Elokus*.

sections.title: I, G-d, do not change: praying to the Essence, not to His attributes
sections.summary: Even the essential *middos* in the *Atzmus* are not the Essence, which is not stuck in being a *chafetz chesed*, so a request can change the will without changing Him. Prayer is therefore to Him and not to His *middos*: not a sob story that plays on His nature, but a request for a kindness He does not owe.

**Like we explained in os yud**: really the *etzem* is the same. As in the *mashal* of the husband and the house: he just wants them to be happy, so changing the room is not really a change, only a change in the way it is measured out. Or the teacher who is sometimes strict and sometimes nice: it is really the same guy, the same *ratzon*, the same *etzem ratzon*. And even if he changed the *ratzon*, it would still be the same guy, because the whole *ratzon* is just him doing it in different ways; from that side it is really all the same. It is as in section 10: the *etzem* is higher than being a *chafetz chesed*, and does not have to come into it. It also has that ability, but it is not stuck in being a *chafetz chesed*.

From the side of the *etzem* there, it does not have to come out *davka* a certain way; He has to make all these *tzimtzumim* (contractions) before it comes out that it should be like this. So if you ask Him to change it, it is not really essential that it be one way rather than the other. First of all, He does not have to be a nice guy. Second, even if He is going to be a nice guy, He can want it in different ways: being nice does not mean He has to want to give this guy shoes; He can want something else, depending on the situation. And even once you know what you want to do, you can have different plans of how to do it. Each level you can change, and it does not affect the higher levels at all, **like explained at length in os yud-alef**.
